nodes.summary: There is a nontrivial element $w$ of the free group on two generators $x, y$ such that some real number $t \ge -2$ is not the trace of $w(A, B)$ for any $A, B \in \mathrm{GL}(2, \mathbb{R})$, where $w(A, B)$ is obtained by substituting $A$ for $x$ and $B$ for $y$.
nodes.title: Mycielski's trace-range question for $\mathrm{GL}(2, \mathbb{R})$ has a negative answer

nodes.summary: For every nontrivial element $w$ of the free group on two generators $x, y$, the set of traces $\operatorname{tr} w(A, B)$, where $A, B$ range over $\mathrm{GL}(2, \mathbb{R})$ and $w(A, B)$ is obtained by substituting $A$ for $x$ and $B$ for $y$, contains the interval $[-2, \infty)$.
nodes.title: Mycielski's trace-range property for $\mathrm{GL}(2, \mathbb{R})$ (Kourovka 16.69(a))

nodes.summary: For every nontrivial element $w$ of the free group $F_2$ on two generators, the word map $\mathrm{PSL}(2, \mathbb{C}) \times \mathrm{PSL}(2, \mathbb{C}) \to \mathrm{PSL}(2, \mathbb{C})$, $(x, y) \mapsto w(x, y)$, is surjective. That is, Mycielski's question has an affirmative answer for $\mathrm{PSL}(2, \mathbb{C})$.
nodes.title: Nontrivial word maps on $\mathrm{PSL}(2, \mathbb{C})$ are surjective (Kourovka 16.68(b))

nodes.summary: The statement, asked about by J. Mycielski, that for every nontrivial element $w$ of the free group $F_2$ on two generators, the word map $\mathrm{PSL}(2, \mathbb{C}) \times \mathrm{PSL}(2, \mathbb{C}) \to \mathrm{PSL}(2, \mathbb{C})$, $(x, y) \mapsto w(x, y)$, is surjective.
nodes.title: Surjectivity of word maps on $\mathrm{PSL}(2, \mathbb{C})$ (Kourovka 16.68(b))

nodes.summary: There is a nontrivial element $w$ of the free group $F_2$ on two generators whose word map $\mathrm{PSL}(2, \mathbb{R}) \times \mathrm{PSL}(2, \mathbb{R}) \to \mathrm{PSL}(2, \mathbb{R})$, $(x, y) \mapsto w(x, y)$, is not surjective. That is, Mycielski's question has a negative answer for $\mathrm{PSL}(2, \mathbb{R})$.
nodes.title: Some nontrivial word map on $\mathrm{PSL}(2, \mathbb{R})$ is not surjective (Kourovka 16.68(a))

nodes.summary: The statement, asked about by J. Mycielski, that for every nontrivial element $w$ of the free group $F_2$ on two generators, the word map $\mathrm{PSL}(2, \mathbb{R}) \times \mathrm{PSL}(2, \mathbb{R}) \to \mathrm{PSL}(2, \mathbb{R})$, $(x, y) \mapsto w(x, y)$, is surjective.
nodes.title: Surjectivity of word maps on $\mathrm{PSL}(2, \mathbb{R})$ (Kourovka 16.68(a))

nodes.summary: There is a nontrivial element $w$ of the free group on two generators $x, y$ such that some real number $t$ with $-5/27 \le t \le 1$ is not the real part of $w(p, q)$ for any nonzero real quaternions $p, q$, where $w(p, q)$ is obtained by substituting $p$ for $x$ and $q$ for $y$.
nodes.title: Mycielski's real-part question for quaternion word maps has a negative answer

nodes.summary: For every nontrivial element $w$ of the free group on two generators $x, y$, the set of real parts $\operatorname{Re} w(p, q)$, where $p, q$ range over the nonzero real quaternions and $w(p, q)$ is obtained by substituting $p$ for $x$ and $q$ for $y$, contains the interval $[-5/27, 1]$.
nodes.title: Mycielski's real-part property for quaternion word maps (Kourovka 16.69(b))

nodes.summary: There is a nontrivial element $w$ of the free group $F_2$ on two generators whose word map $\mathrm{SO}(3, \mathbb{R}) \times \mathrm{SO}(3, \mathbb{R}) \to \mathrm{SO}(3, \mathbb{R})$, $(x, y) \mapsto w(x, y)$, is not surjective. That is, Mycielski's question has a negative answer for $\mathrm{SO}(3, \mathbb{R})$.
nodes.title: Some nontrivial word map on $\mathrm{SO}(3, \mathbb{R})$ is not surjective (Kourovka 16.68(c))

nodes.summary: The statement, asked about by J. Mycielski, that for every nontrivial element $w$ of the free group $F_2$ on two generators, the word map $\mathrm{SO}(3, \mathbb{R}) \times \mathrm{SO}(3, \mathbb{R}) \to \mathrm{SO}(3, \mathbb{R})$, $(x, y) \mapsto w(x, y)$, is surjective.
nodes.title: Surjectivity of word maps on $\mathrm{SO}(3, \mathbb{R})$ (Kourovka 16.68(c))

nodes.summary: For a group $G$ and an element $w$ of the free group $F_2$ on two generators $x_0, x_1$, the word map of $w$ is the map $G \times G \to G$ sending $(x, y)$ to $w(x, y)$, the image of $w$ under the group homomorphism $F_2 \to G$ with $x_0 \mapsto x$ and $x_1 \mapsto y$.
nodes.title: Word map

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
